Irregular verbs

VV2for Present PerfectV3
goWe go to school.wentI went there yesterday.goneWe have just gone home.
eatHe eats lunch.ateHe ate pizza last night.eatenHe has already eaten his lunch.
seeThey see the sea.sawThey saw a bird yesterday.seenShe has never seen a rainbow.
doShe does her homework.didShe did her homework two days ago.doneThey have just done their homework.
haveYou have a bike.hadWe had lunch yesterday.hadI have never had a pet.
makeDad makes tea.madeDad made soup last night.madeDad has just made dinner.
takeI take the bus.tookI took it two days ago.takenShe has already taken the bus.
writeShe writes stories.wroteShe wrote a letter last week.writtenI have just written a letter.
buyWe buy fruit.boughtWe bought fruit yesterday.boughtWe have just bought some fruit.
comeThey come home.cameThey came home last night.comeThey have just come home.
giveHe gives gifts.gaveHe gave me a book yesterday.givenHe has already given me the book.
beThey are happy.was / wereWe were happy yesterday.beenShe has never been to London.
getI get up early.gotI got up early this morning.got / gottenWe have just got home.
readHe reads books.readI read this book two days ago.readHe has already read this book.
drinkWe drink water.drankShe drank tea yesterday.drunkShe has never drunk coffee.
beginClass begins at nine.beganClass began at nine yesterday.begunThe film has just begun.
breakHe breaks toys.brokeHe broke his toy last week.brokenHe has just broken his toy.
bringShe brings her bag.broughtShe brought her bag yesterday.broughtShe has already brought her bag.
findI find new words.foundI found my keys last night.foundI have just found my keys.
feelThey feel tired.feltThey felt tired yesterday.feltThey have never felt so happy.
leaveThe bus leaves at eight.leftThe bus left ten minutes ago.leftThe bus has already left.
meetWe meet on Fridays.metWe met at school yesterday.metWe have just met our new teacher.
sleepMy cat sleeps a lot.sleptMy cat slept all morning.sleptMy cat has already slept today.
speakHe speaks English.spokeHe spoke to me yesterday.spokenHe has never spoken to her.
swimWe swim on Sundays.swamWe swam in the sea last summer.swumShe has never swum in the sea.
knowShe knows the answer.knewShe knew the answer in class yesterday.knownI've known him for two years.
thinkI think it's nice.thoughtI thought about it last night.thoughtShe has never thought about it.
runThey run every day.ranThey ran to school yesterday.runHe has already run five kilometres.
sayHe says hello.saidHe said hello this morning.saidHe has just said goodbye.
tellShe tells a story.toldShe told a story last night.toldShe has never told a lie.
loseHe often loses his keys.lostI lost my keys yesterday.lostI have just lost my keys.
hearWe hear music.heardWe heard music last night.heardWe have never heard this song.
wearShe wears a coat.woreShe wore a coat yesterday.wornShe has never worn that dress.

✎ V = base form · V2 = Past Simple · V3 = with have / has / had

☾ Past Simple ✦

Yesterday. Last week. Many years ago. ⏳ A story that is finished!

A 🎻 A story from the past

We use Past Simple for finished actions in the past.

🎼 Mozart wrote wonderful music.
🎵 He lived many years ago.
🗓️ He died in 1791.

Those actions happened in the past. They are finished.

🌙 yesterday📅 last week⏰ two days ago

B ✍️ Regular & irregular

Most regular verbs end in -ed. Some change spelling. Irregular verbs are different.

walk → walkedstudy → studiedstop → stopped

✨ Irregular verbs

write → wrotesee → sawgo → wentshut → shut
🍰 We made a cake yesterday.

C ❓ Did & didn't

In questions, use Did + person + base verb?

🎉 Did you enjoy the party?
📚 What did she read?

In negative sentences, use didn't + base verb.

🥕 I didn't eat the carrots.
💡 Say: Did you go? — NOT “Did you went?”
✅ Yes, I did.❌ No, I didn't.

D 🌦️ Was & were

The past of am / is / are is was / were.

🙋 I / he / she / it → was👫 you / we / they → were
🛋️ I was at home yesterday.
☁️ They were outside.
🌻 She wasn't tired.
🌞 Were you happy? — Yes, I was.

For be, ask: Was she…? or Were they…? — not “Did she be…?”
